notice: SYNTHETIC AND FICTIONAL. 'Velora', 'Northland' and 'Southmark' do not exist. Nothing here is law of India or of any state; amounts are invented and use the fictional unit VEL. Use only to benchmark retrieval mechanics.

provisions.heading: Section 1. Short title and definitions
provisions.text: (1) This Act may be called the Velora Road Traffic Act, 2001. (2) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires, "motor vehicle" means any mechanically propelled vehicle adapted for use upon roads; "transport vehicle" means a goods carriage, a contract carriage or a stage carriage used for hire or reward; "learner" means a person who holds a learner's licence issued under section 2; and "licensing authority" means an authority empowered by the State Government to issue licences under this Act.

provisions.heading: Section 2. Necessity for driving licence
provisions.text: (1) No person shall drive a motor vehicle in any public place unless he holds an effective driving licence issued to him authorising him to drive the vehicle. (2) A learner may drive a motor vehicle only while displaying the letter L on the front and rear of the vehicle and while accompanied by an instructor who holds an effective driving licence for that class of vehicle. (3) No owner or person in charge of a motor vehicle shall cause or permit any person who does not satisfy sub-section (1) to drive the vehicle.

provisions.heading: Section 3. Age limit in connection with driving
provisions.text: (1) No person under the age of eighteen years shall drive a motor vehicle in any public place. (2) A person who has attained the age of sixteen years may drive a gearless motor cycle with an engine capacity not exceeding fifty cubic centimetres. (3) No person under the age of twenty years shall drive a transport vehicle in any public place.

provisions.heading: Section 4. Necessity for registration
provisions.text: (1) No person shall drive any motor vehicle and no owner shall cause or permit the vehicle to be driven in any public place unless the vehicle is registered and the certificate of registration has not been suspended or cancelled. (2) A dealer may grant temporary registration valid for a period not exceeding thirty days so that the owner can apply for permanent registration. (3) A vehicle brought from another State may be kept for up to twelve months before a new registration mark must be assigned.

provisions.heading: Section 5. Necessity for insurance against third party risk
provisions.text: (1) No person shall use a motor vehicle in a public place unless there is in force in relation to the use of the vehicle a policy of insurance covering liability to third parties. (2) Every policy shall cover death of or bodily injury to any person, including the owner of goods carried, and damage to third-party property. (3) The certificate of insurance shall be carried in the vehicle in physical or electronic form.

provisions.heading: Section 6. Limits of speed
provisions.text: (1) The Central Government may fix the maximum speed for any class of vehicle on expressways, which shall not exceed one hundred and twenty kilometres per hour. (2) Subject to sub-section (1), the State Government may by notification fix maximum and minimum speeds for any area or road within the State. (3) Speed limits shall be shown by traffic signs placed at suitable points.

provisions.heading: Section 7. Protective headgear
provisions.text: (1) Every person driving or riding a two-wheeled motor cycle, including the pillion rider, shall wear protective headgear conforming to the standards notified by the Central Government. (2) The headgear shall be securely fastened to the head of the wearer by means of straps. (3) A person holding a certificate from a registered medical practitioner that wearing headgear is unsafe for him on medical grounds is exempt from sub-section (1).

provisions.heading: Section 8. Safety belts and child restraints
provisions.text: (1) The driver and every passenger of a motor car shall wear a safety belt while the vehicle is in motion. (2) A child below the age of fourteen years shall be secured by a safety belt or, where the child is below four years, by a child restraint system appropriate to the child's weight. (3) The owner shall ensure that seat belts are fitted and in working order for every seat.

provisions.heading: Section 9. Driving by a drunken person
provisions.text: (1) Whoever, while driving a motor vehicle, has in his blood alcohol exceeding thirty milligrams per hundred millilitres of blood, detected in a test by a breath analyser, commits an offence. (2) A police officer in uniform may require any person driving a motor vehicle to provide a sample of breath if he has reasonable cause to suspect that the person has consumed alcohol. (3) Refusal to provide a breath sample without reasonable excuse shall be treated as an offence under sub-section (1).

provisions.heading: Section 10. Schedule of penalties
provisions.text: The penalties for offences under this Act are as follows. General offence for which no penalty is otherwise provided: 500 VEL for a first offence and 1,500 VEL for a subsequent offence. Driving without a valid driving licence (section 2): 5,000 VEL. Driving a light motor vehicle above the speed limit (section 6): 1,000 VEL to 2,000 VEL. Driving by a drunken person (section 9): 10,000 VEL or imprisonment up to six months for a first offence, and 15,000 VEL or imprisonment up to two years for a subsequent offence. Using a vehicle without third-party insurance (section 5): 2,000 VEL, and 4,000 VEL for a subsequent offence. Riding without protective headgear (section 7): 1,000 VEL and disqualification from holding a licence for three months. Not wearing a safety belt (section 8): 1,000 VEL.

provisions.heading: Section 11. Compounding of offences
provisions.text: (1) Any offence punishable under sections 2, 5, 6, 7 or 8 may, either before or after the institution of the prosecution, be compounded by such officers and for such amounts as the State Government may by notification specify. (2) Where an offence is compounded, the offender, if in custody, shall be discharged and no further proceedings shall be taken against him. (3) An offence under section 9 shall not be compounded.

provisions.heading: Section 12. Duty of driver in case of accident
provisions.text: (1) When any person is injured or any property of a third party is damaged as a result of an accident in which a motor vehicle is involved, the driver shall take all reasonable steps to secure medical attention for the injured person by conveying him to the nearest medical practitioner or hospital. (2) The driver shall give information about the accident to the nearest police station within twenty-four hours of its occurrence. (3) The driver shall give any information required by the injured person or a police officer.

provisions.heading: Section 13. Claims tribunals and application for compensation
provisions.text: (1) The State Government may constitute one or more Motor Accidents Claims Tribunals for adjudicating claims for compensation arising out of accidents involving motor vehicles. (2) An application for compensation may be made by the injured person, the owner of damaged property, or the legal representatives of a deceased person. (3) No application for compensation shall be entertained unless it is made within six months of the occurrence of the accident.

provisions.heading: Section 14. Protection of Good Samaritans
provisions.text: (1) A Good Samaritan who in good faith, voluntarily and without expectation of payment, renders emergency medical or non-medical assistance at the scene of an accident shall not be liable for any civil or criminal action for any injury to or death of the victim resulting from his negligence in acting or failing to act. (2) A Good Samaritan shall not be compelled to disclose his name or contact details to the police or hospital.

documents.title: The Velora Central Motor Vehicle Rules, 2002

provisions.heading: Rule 1. Application for learner's licence
provisions.text: (1) An application for a learner's licence shall be made in Form LL-1 to the licensing authority together with proof of age and address and a fee of 150 VEL. (2) The applicant shall pass a test of knowledge of traffic signs and road safety. (3) A learner's licence shall be valid for six months from the date of issue.

provisions.heading: Rule 2. Renewal of driving licence
provisions.text: (1) An application for renewal of a driving licence shall be made in Form DL-9 not earlier than one year before and not later than one year after its expiry. (2) Where the applicant has attained the age of forty years, the application shall be accompanied by a medical certificate in Form MC-1. (3) If the application is made more than one year after expiry, the applicant shall pass the test of competence to drive again.

provisions.heading: Rule 3. Pollution under control certificate
provisions.text: (1) Every motor vehicle shall carry a valid pollution under control certificate issued by an authorised testing station. (2) The certificate shall be valid for six months, except that for a new vehicle the first certificate shall be valid for one year from the date of first registration. (3) Emission readings shall be uploaded to the national vehicle database by the testing station.

provisions.heading: Rule 4. Registration plates
provisions.text: (1) Every motor vehicle shall display high security registration plates affixed by an authorised manufacturer. (2) Private vehicles shall display black letters on a white background, transport vehicles black letters on a yellow background, and battery electric vehicles white letters on a green background. (3) No decoration, sticker or name other than the registration mark shall be displayed on the plate.

provisions.heading: Rule 5. Certificate of fitness for transport vehicles
provisions.text: (1) A transport vehicle shall not be deemed validly registered unless it carries a certificate of fitness. (2) The certificate of fitness shall be renewed every two years for the first eight years from registration and every year thereafter. (3) Fitness testing shall be carried out at an automated testing station where one has been notified.

provisions.heading: Rule 6. Safety glass and tinting
provisions.text: (1) The windscreen and windows of every motor car shall be of safety glass. (2) The visual light transmission of the glass shall be not less than seventy per cent for the front windscreen and rear window and not less than fifty per cent for the side windows. (3) No film or other material shall be pasted on the glass to reduce transmission below these limits.

provisions.heading: Rule 7. Documents in electronic form
provisions.text: (1) A certificate of registration, insurance, fitness, permit, driving licence or pollution under control certificate presented in electronic form through Velora DocVault shall be treated as equivalent to the physical document. (2) An enforcement officer shall not seize a physical document where its electronic form has been verified through DocVault, except where the document is required for investigation.

provisions.heading: Rule 8. Transfer of ownership
provisions.text: (1) Where ownership of a registered vehicle is transferred within the same State, the transferor and transferee shall report the transfer in Forms TO-29 and TO-30 within fourteen days. (2) Where the vehicle is to be used in another State, the report shall be made within forty-five days. (3) The registering authority shall enter the transfer in the certificate of registration and the national vehicle database.

provisions.heading: Rule 1. Speed limits in Northland
provisions.text: In exercise of the powers under section 6 of the Act, the maximum speed in Northland shall be fifty kilometres per hour for motor cars and forty kilometres per hour for motor cycles within municipal limits, and ninety kilometres per hour on state highways. Near schools and hospitals the maximum speed shall be twenty-five kilometres per hour.

provisions.heading: Rule 2. Compounding fees in Northland
provisions.text: Under section 11 of the Act, the following amounts are specified for compounding in Northland: riding without protective headgear, 500 VEL; not wearing a safety belt, 500 VEL; driving without a driving licence, 2,000 VEL; over-speeding in a light motor vehicle, 1,500 VEL; using a vehicle without insurance, 2,000 VEL. Officers of the rank of sub-inspector of police and above, and motor vehicle inspectors, may compound these offences.

provisions.heading: Rule 3. Road tax in Northland
provisions.text: (1) A one-time road tax shall be levied on registration at six per cent of the cost of a two-wheeler and eight per cent of the cost of a motor car. (2) Battery electric vehicles registered before the thirty-first day of March 2030 are exempt from road tax. (3) Tax shall be paid at the registering authority before the registration mark is assigned.

provisions.heading: Rule 4. Parking and towing in Northland
provisions.text: (1) No vehicle shall be parked within fifteen metres of a road junction or in front of any hospital entrance. (2) A vehicle parked in contravention of this rule may be towed away, and the owner shall pay towing charges of 600 VEL in addition to any compounding fee before the vehicle is released.

provisions.heading: Rule 5. Registering authorities in Northland
provisions.text: The Regional Transport Officer, Harbor City, shall be the registering authority for Harbor City district, and the Regional Transport Officer, Pinefield, for Pinefield and Lakeview districts. Applications for registration, transfer and duplicate certificates shall be made to the officer having jurisdiction where the owner resides.

provisions.heading: Rule 6. Autorickshaw permits in Northland
provisions.text: (1) The number of autorickshaw permits in Harbor City shall not exceed twenty thousand. (2) A permit shall be granted only for a vehicle running on compressed natural gas or battery power. (3) A permit holder shall display a fare chart approved by the Regional Transport Authority inside the vehicle.

provisions.heading: Rule 7. Restriction on heavy goods vehicles in Harbor City
provisions.text: Heavy goods vehicles shall not enter the municipal limits of Harbor City between eight in the morning and ten at night, except vehicles carrying perishable goods, fuel or emergency supplies with a pass issued by the traffic police.

provisions.heading: Rule 1. Speed limits in Southmark
provisions.text: In exercise of the powers under section 6 of the Act, the maximum speed in Southmark shall be sixty kilometres per hour for motor cars and fifty kilometres per hour for motor cycles within municipal limits, and one hundred kilometres per hour on four-lane state highways. Near schools the maximum speed shall be thirty kilometres per hour during school hours.

provisions.heading: Rule 2. Compounding fees in Southmark
provisions.text: Under section 11 of the Act, the following amounts are specified for compounding in Southmark: riding without protective headgear, 1,000 VEL; not wearing a safety belt, 1,000 VEL; driving without a driving licence, 5,000 VEL; over-speeding in a light motor vehicle, 2,000 VEL. Compounding may be done by traffic police officers of the rank of head constable and above through the e-challan system.

provisions.heading: Rule 3. Road tax in Southmark
provisions.text: (1) Road tax shall be levied at eight per cent of the cost for two-wheelers and twelve per cent of the cost for motor cars, payable once at the time of registration. (2) Battery electric vehicles shall be entitled to a concession of fifty per cent of the road tax. (3) Vehicles registered in another State and brought into Southmark shall pay tax proportionate to the remaining life of the vehicle.

provisions.heading: Rule 4. Parking and towing in Southmark
provisions.text: (1) No vehicle shall be parked within ten metres of a road junction, on a footpath or near a fire hydrant. (2) A towed vehicle shall be released only on payment of towing charges of 1,000 VEL for a car and 400 VEL for a two-wheeler.

provisions.heading: Rule 5. Learner's licence test in Southmark
provisions.text: (1) The test of knowledge for a learner's licence may be taken online from home through the Southmark Transport Portal using face authentication. (2) An applicant who fails the test may retake it after seven days. (3) Applicants who do not have access to the online facility may take the test at any Regional Transport Office.

provisions.heading: Rule 6. Child passengers on two-wheelers in Southmark
provisions.text: (1) A child aged between nine months and four years carried on a motor cycle shall wear a crash helmet of suitable size and shall be secured to the driver by a safety harness. (2) A motor cycle carrying a child below four years shall not be driven at a speed exceeding forty kilometres per hour.

provisions.heading: Rule 7. Hit-and-run relief scheme in Southmark
provisions.text: (1) The victim of a hit-and-run accident in Southmark, or his legal representative, shall be paid interim relief of 25,000 VEL for grievous hurt and 75,000 VEL in case of death. (2) The claim shall be made to the District Collector within six months with a copy of the first information report.
